A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adaptive Low-Pass Guidance (ALG) work despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete included appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation evaluations, component studies, feature visualizations, runtime measurements, and a five-seed CogVideoX experiment.

after.justification: v2 reports original evaluations across three datasets, model comparisons, prompt-augmentation experiments, component studies, qualitative examples, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The core ALG guidance equation and adaptive filtering procedure remain. v2 adds limited inference refinements: delaying filtered conditioning with initial clean-conditioning steps and replacing the first-frame latent before decoding. Appendix A and Table 7 specify delaying for Wan 2.2 and first-frame replacement for Wan 2.1/2.2.

E1.justification: v2 adds quantitative coverage of real video frames from PVD and VidProM prompts paired with FLUX.1-dev images, substantially extending v1's VBench-centered evaluation. Synthetic inputs already appeared in v1 Appendix C.1.3, so that input type itself is not new. v2 also excludes background-only VBench cases and removes the Sora demonstration comparison.

E2.justification: CFG remains the principal comparator. v2 Table 4 adds CFG with Gemini-generated motion-augmented prompts as an evaluated alternative, alongside ALG with and without augmentation. The qualitative comparison against OpenAI Sora demonstrations in v1 Appendix C.1.2 disappears.

E3.justification: VBench evaluation changes from 355 to 246 pairs, while component studies change from a 100-prompt subset to the stated full evaluation set. Main evaluations replace CogVideoX/HunyuanVideo with Wan 2.2, retaining Wan 2.1/LTX-Video. v2 introduces DOVER, VisionReward, and aggregate VBench scores, drops raw optical-flow and background metrics, and changes the stated default transition time from 0.06 to 0.1. New dataset construction and prompt augmentation introduce further protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds the prompt-augmentation study testing complementarity with ALG, but removes v1's step-versus-exponential schedule comparison. Transition-time, filter-strength, filter-type, and shortcut diagnostics remain, although some settings and metrics change. The guidance-design failure examples and additional feature maps are retained under new figure numbers.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix C.2.1 reports CogVideoX results averaged over five seeds, supplementing single-seed main evaluations. v2 removes this check and describes single-seed evaluations throughout Sections 4–5. Neither version reports confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests; the change removes a limited repeated-seed validation.

E6.justification: Main-table CFG/ALG Dynamic Degree scores change from 28.9/41.5 to 28.9/39.4 for Wan 2.1 and from 12.6/21.1 to 15.5/21.5 for LTX-Video. v2 adds Wan 2.2 results, including 31.7/39.0 on VBench, extensive PVD/VidProM results, and prompt-augmentation outcomes. CogVideoX/HunyuanVideo main results and five-seed results disappear. These are revised or additional results under changed conditions, not direct same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: v2 removes the explicitly defined exponential alternative kappa(t) = kappa* exp(-lambda t) from v1 Section 3.2. The general ALG formulation, CFG equations, step-function schedule, and guidance decomposition remain substantively unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central motion-suppression diagnosis and training-free ALG contribution remain. v2 modestly strengthens the abstract/introduction claims from preserving fidelity and quality to sometimes improving them, and updates the headline average dynamic-degree improvement from 36% to 33% for the revised evaluation.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit limitations concerning inherited model biases and model-dependent optimal hyperparameters, along with the explanation that subjects leaving the frame can lower consistency scores. It adds interpretations of prompt augmentation as complementary to ALG and delayed filtering as trading slightly less motion for better quality. The main shortcut explanation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents Wan 2.2 integration and checkpoints, per-model override/delay settings, construction of the new evaluation datasets, and the exact Gemini augmentation instruction. It adds a structured prompt/model table and updates hardware reporting from H100/A100 to H200/H100. CogVideoX/HunyuanVideo implementation details are removed. The abstract newly directs readers to source code through the existing project page.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands literature coverage with newer video-generation systems, including MAGI-1, Self Forcing, FramePack, and FlashI2V, plus the added datasets and evaluators. Section 2 explicitly discusses FlashI2V's latent shifting and Fourier guidance relative to ALG. References supporting the removed Sora, GPT-4o, and DreamSim material disappear.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, wording is polished, Section 5 becomes 'Analysis,' and experimental and appendix prose is selectively reorganized. Prompt information becomes Appendix B.4, and qualitative-result subsections are consolidated. The main introduction–background–method–experiments–analysis–conclusion sequence and much explanatory prose remain.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one to two columns. Introductory figures are redesigned, qualitative galleries are substantially rearranged, and main tables emphasize aggregate metrics with detailed results consolidated in appendix Table 9. Ablation plots change their displayed quality metrics. Some existing visualizations are simply retained and renumbered, including v1 Figures 12, 14–15 as v2 Figures 7, 9–10.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the mainly VBench-based quantitative evidence with PVD/VidProM evaluations, additional quality evaluators, and a prompt-augmentation control, improving support for the motion–quality tradeoff across varied inputs. Clearer implementation instructions also help reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removing the five-seed check, CogVideoX/HunyuanVideo main evaluations, alternative-schedule evidence, and explicit limitations.
